$comment: The E-Myth Revisited (Gerber, 1995) — probes. Target: L8.3 (delivery capacity), L8.1 (time-for-money), sistemisasi.

probes.text: If you are sick for 2 weeks and cannot work at all, what happens to your income and your clients’ work — honestly?

signal_interpretation.positive: There is a system/person who can replace — the business does not depend on an individual
signal_interpretation.negative: Pendapatan berhenti total & pekerjaan tertunda — 100% tergantung satu orang
signal_interpretation.neutral: Some can be diverted — semi-finished system

probes.text: Your routine work (revisions, client onboarding, reports) — is there a step-by-step document that others can follow, or is it all just in your head?

signal_interpretation.positive: There is a written SOP in use — it can be delegated.
signal_interpretation.negative: All in your head — every new client necessarily adds to your hours

probes.text: Before taking on a new client, have you ever calculated beforehand: how many hours/week they need AND where those hours will be taken from?

signal_interpretation.positive: Capacity is calculated before commit — client acceptance is controlled
signal_interpretation.negative: Accept first, find time later — capacity quietly collapses.

probes.text: If today you had to work 2× less, which work do you think does NOT need to be done at all — and why are you still doing it?

signal_interpretation.positive: Able to distinguish valuable vs non-valuable work + has a systemic rationale
signal_interpretation.negative: Semua terasa wajib & dilakukan sendiri — tanda technician-dominan
signal_interpretation.neutral: Knowing something is wasteful but hesitant to stop
